name: B10-0205/2026 (PfE) – The need for targeted criminal provisions and platforms’ responsibility to effectively address cyberbullying and online harassment
title: JOINT MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the need for targeted criminal provisions and platforms’ responsibility to effectively address cyberbullying and online harassment
part_text:
**What it asks for:** This is an opinion, not a law. The European Parliament says countries, not the European Union, should mainly handle online bullying through their own criminal laws and school lessons. It asks countries to punish sharing intimate images without consent, including threats to do so. It asks platforms to remove such images fast, stop re-uploads, and give users easy reporting and blocking tools. It also warns against mandatory digital identity checks and scanning private messages.

**What concretely changes:** Nothing yet. It only states Parliament's position and asks countries and platforms to act.

**Who it affects:** Children and young people online, their parents, and social media platforms.

**What happens next:** Parliament sends the text to the Council, the Commission and national governments. No binding rules follow from it.
